1) Some of this goes back to WW1. The short is that Germany was becoming a rival to England. WW1 was started as a war between Austria and Serbia yet at the end of the entire thing Germany had to pay off the war costs of every participant.... Churchill's position and the position of the British government was that the goal of the war was to smash Germany. Germany was a growing industrial economy and the British economy had shifted increasingly towards banking and trade. When Germany started to rebuild after Hitler took power they did two things that pissed off the British. One was refuse to continue payments of the Versailles treaty (which was always absurd to begin with) and second was they began to issue government-backed money that wasn't tied to a private central bank. In doing this, the Germans were taking the first step to pull out of the so-called 'global finance system', a system which at the time (and still is to a large degree) a major component of the British economy.

2) They used an almost limitless supply of money to influence the course of the war and at the same time profit immensely from it. I could expand on this with specifics but it would take time.

4) This one is complicated and a bit more controversial. Some important history needs to be recognized. One thing is that Poland did not exist between 1795-1918. For those 173 years Polish territory belonged to Prussia, Russia and Austria-Hungary. Poland had to play a complicated and difficult diplomatic game with the USSR, Germany and its other neighbours just to continue to exist, and border conflicts were fairly common. Hitler had actually offered Poland an alliance with Germany against the USSR on several occasions, but they declined. Hitler didn't really seem to know what to make of this, since the Polish leaders were nationalists who had also just ended a war of their own against soviet Russia (Polish-Soviet war). Instead, Poland made the mistake of allying itself with France. Apparently Poland was even discussing a pre-emptive war with France against Germany (although this isn't confirmed and is part of the controversy). Poland signed non-aggression treaties with both the USSR (which made Germany nervous) and Germany, and kept an alliance with France. To add fuel to this tension, a number of disputes were constantly erupting between ethnic Poles and ethnic Germans. One focal point of the tensions was a city called the 'Free city of Danzig", technically part of Polish territory but administered as a sort of autonomous city with a major German population. As part of Hitler's plan to reunify the German people and undo the treaty or versailles damages, Hitler asked to return Danzig to Germany. The Polish government refused, Hitler felt he couldn't trust the Polish government to not ally with the USSR against him and so basically decided 'f it' and invaded Danzig. Poland held out briefly and waited for the French and British to send the reinforcements they had promised. Nobody came, and Germany and USSR both took the country. France and Britain waged the 'phoney war', Germany tried to negotiate an end to that situation (since it didn't even really look like France or Britain wanted to fight the war, since they didn't send any troops or actually do anything, and Germany gave them a few months to find a diplomatic solution). So the British and French seemed to have used the alliance with Poland to goad Poland into standing up to Germany when they had no plan at all to actually help Poland, nor did they have any plans to do anything about the Soviets invading Poland.
